title: Formatting entomological data with format_eht_data()
text: Entomological hut trial (EHT) data often comes various sources inconsistent naming. Different teams may use: Different column names variables (e.g., UnfedAlive, UF.alive, u_alive, UA) Different cases (e.g., Treatment, treatment, TREATMENT) Different treatment encodings (e.g., character labels vs. numeric codes) format_eht_data() function standardizes data inconsistencies.

title: Formatting entomological data with format_eht_data()
text: Standardizes column names: Maps common variations standard names (UA, UD, FA, FD, treatment, etc.) Coerces data types: Converts endpoints numeric Encodes treatments: Converts treatment labels numeric encoding (0 = control, 1+ = treatments), keeping labels vector_control_product label results Calculates variables: Adds fed, dead, total columns

text: package supports custom models four mechanisms: Custom Stan file: Provide path .stan file Custom Stan data: Provide data list matching model’s requirements Custom parameters: Specify parameters extract Custom initialization: Provide initialization function

what: Example 1: Simple Custom Model with Additional Parameter
title: Workflow: Using Custom Stan Models
text: Let’s create custom model includes additional parameter net age effect.

previous_headings: Example 1: Simple Custom Model with Additional Parameter
title: Workflow: Using Custom Stan Models
text: Create file custom_model_net_age.stan:
code: // Custom EHT model with net age covariate functions {   real P_UA(real alpha, real mu) {     return exp(-(alpha + mu));   }   real P_F(real alpha, real mu) {     return (1 - P_UA(alpha, mu)) * alpha / (alpha + mu);   }   real P_UD(real alpha, real mu) {     return (1 - P_UA(alpha, mu)) * mu / (alpha + mu);   }   real P_FA(real alpha, real mu, real PC) {     return P_F(alpha, mu) * PC;   }   real P_FD(real alpha, real mu, real PC) {     return P_F(alpha, mu) * (1 - PC);   } }  data {   int<lower=0> N;                // number of observations   int<lower=0> tr;               // number of treatments   array[N] int treat;            // treatment index   array[N, 4] int<lower=0> y;    // outcomes (UA, UD, FA, FD)   vector[N] net_age;             // net age in months (NEW!)   int<lower=0, upper=1> use_likelihood; }  parameters {   vector<lower=0, upper=1>[tr+1] PostprandialKilling;   vector<lower=0>[tr+1] KillingDuringHostSeeking;   vector<lower=0, upper=1>[tr+1] HostAvailabilityReduction;    // NEW: Net age decay parameter   real<lower=0> net_age_decay;    real a;   real m;   real b; }  transformed parameters {   real<lower=0> alpha_0 = exp(a);   real<lower=0> mu_0 = exp(m);   real<lower=0, upper=1> pC_0 = inv_logit(b); }  model {   matrix[4, N] theta;    // Priors   target += uniform_lpdf(PostprandialKilling | 0, 1);   target += lognormal_lpdf(1 - HostAvailabilityReduction | 0, 5);   target += lognormal_lpdf(KillingDuringHostSeeking | 0, 5);    // Prior for net age decay (half-normal)   target += normal_lpdf(net_age_decay | 0, 0.1) - normal_lccdf(0 | 0, 0.1);    target += normal_lpdf(a | 0, 6);   target += normal_lpdf(m | 0, 6);   target += logistic_lpdf(b | 0, 1);    // Likelihood   for (i in 1:N) {     // Calculate decay factor based on net age     real decay_factor = exp(-net_age_decay * net_age[i]);      if (treat[i] == 0) {       theta[1, i] = P_UA(alpha_0, mu_0);       theta[2, i] = P_UD(alpha_0, mu_0);       theta[3, i] = P_FA(alpha_0, mu_0, pC_0);       theta[4, i] = P_FD(alpha_0, mu_0, pC_0);     } else {       // Apply efficacy with decay       real eff_availability = HostAvailabilityReduction[treat[i]+1] * decay_factor;       real eff_killing = KillingDuringHostSeeking[treat[i]+1] * decay_factor;       real eff_postprandial = PostprandialKilling[treat[i]+1] * decay_factor;        real alpha_i = (1 - eff_availability) * alpha_0;       real mu_i = mu_0 + eff_killing * alpha_0;       real pCi = pC_0 * (1 - eff_postprandial);        theta[1, i] = P_UA(alpha_i, mu_i);       theta[2, i] = P_UD(alpha_i, mu_i);       theta[3, i] = P_FA(alpha_i, mu_i, pCi);       theta[4, i] = P_FD(alpha_i, mu_i, pCi);     }      if (use_likelihood == 1)       target += multinomial_lpmf(y[i, ] | theta[, i]);   } }  generated quantities {   // Compute half-life of net effectiveness   real net_halflife = log(2) / net_age_decay;    // Other derived quantities as needed }

title: Workflow: Using Custom Stan Models
code: // Binary outcome model: alive vs dead data {   int<lower=0> N;   array[N] int<lower=0> n_alive;    // Number alive   array[N] int<lower=0> n_total;    // Total mosquitoes   array[N] int treat;   int<lower=0> tr; }  parameters {   real<lower=0, upper=1> baseline_survival;   vector<lower=0, upper=1>[tr] mortality_effect; }  model {   // Priors   baseline_survival ~ beta(5, 2);   mortality_effect ~ beta(2, 2);    // Likelihood   for (i in 1:N) {     real p_alive;     if (treat[i] == 0) {       p_alive = baseline_survival;     } else {       p_alive = baseline_survival * (1 - mortality_effect[treat[i]]);     }     n_alive[i] ~ binomial(n_total[i], p_alive);   } }

title: Workflow: Using Predefined Models
text: semifield model follows workflow, model_type = "semifield" data listed Step 1. basic model, simulate dataset similar repellent experiment Denz et al. (2021), effects estimated article, refit model.
code: set.seed(1) n_nights <- 20     # matched nights released <- 100    # mosquitoes released per arm and night true_semifield <- c(HostAvailabilityReduction = 0.416, KillingDuringHostSeeking = 0.911)  # Night-specific control rates (per hour), with night-to-night variation alpha <- exp(log(0.3) + rnorm(n_nights, 0, 0.3)) mu    <- exp(log(0.05) + rnorm(n_nights, 0, 0.3))  # Outcome probabilities H1, H2, H3, H4, L (no trap) semifield_probs <- function(alpha, mu) {   PA <- function(t) exp(-(alpha + mu) * t)   PH <- function(t) (1 - PA(t)) * alpha / (alpha + mu)   p <- c(PH(1), PA(1) * PH(1), PA(1)^2 * PH(1), PA(1)^3 * PH(9))   c(p, 1 - sum(p)) }  # Outcome matrices of matched nights (one row per night, same order in both arms); # without a trap, the T column can be left out semifield_data <- list(   y0 = t(sapply(1:n_nights, function(k)     rmultinom(1, released, semifield_probs(alpha[k], mu[k])))),   y1 = t(sapply(1:n_nights, function(k)     rmultinom(1, released, semifield_probs((1 - true_semifield[[1]]) * alpha[k],                                            mu[k] + true_semifield[[2]] * alpha[k]))))   # if the compartments contained a trap, add its availability per night:   # beta0 = ..., beta1 = ... ) fit_semifield <- fit_ento_model(   data = semifield_data,   model_type = "semifield",   iter = 2000,   warmup = 1000,   chains = 2,   seed = 123,   save_y_rep = TRUE,   refresh = 0 ) #> ℹ Using predefined model: semifield #> ℹ Fitting Stan model... #> ℹ Iterations: 2000 | Warmup: 1000 | Chains: 2 #> ✔ Model fitting complete  # Estimates and true values extract_stan_summary(fit_semifield) #> # A tibble: 2 × 5 #>   param                     treatment  mean lower upper #>   <chr>                         <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 KillingDuringHostSeeking         NA 0.934 0.815 1.06  #> 2 HostAvailabilityReduction        NA 0.383 0.305 0.454 true_semifield #> HostAvailabilityReduction  KillingDuringHostSeeking  #>                     0.416                     0.911  # Posterior predictive check ppc_semifield <- posterior_predictive_check(fit_semifield, data = semifield_data) plot_posterior_predictive(ppc_semifield)
